vocab.meaning_vi: mang tính giả định, chưa xảy ra thật
vocab.example: This is a hypothetical question, but please answer in detail.
vocab.example_vi: Đây là câu hỏi giả định, nhưng hãy trả lời chi tiết nhé.

vocab.meaning_vi: sắp xếp thứ tự ưu tiên
vocab.example: I prioritise the task that blocks other people first.
vocab.example_vi: Tôi ưu tiên việc đang chặn công việc của người khác trước.

vocab.meaning_vi: sự xung đột giữa các việc ưu tiên
vocab.example: When there is a clash of priorities, I talk to both managers.
vocab.example_vi: Khi có xung đột giữa các việc ưu tiên, tôi trao đổi với cả hai quản lý.

vocab.meaning_vi: suy nghĩ thấu đáo trước khi quyết định
vocab.example: I take five minutes to think it through before I answer.
vocab.example_vi: Tôi dành năm phút suy nghĩ thấu đáo trước khi trả lời.

vocab.meaning_vi: quyết định dựa trên phán đoán cá nhân
vocab.example: It was a judgement call, and I explained my reasons clearly.
vocab.example_vi: Đó là quyết định theo phán đoán cá nhân, và tôi đã giải thích rõ lý do.

vocab.meaning_vi: nêu vấn đề sớm, không để muộn
vocab.example: If I see a risk, I raise it early with my manager.
vocab.example_vi: Nếu thấy rủi ro, tôi nêu vấn đề sớm với quản lý của mình.

vocab.example: In the worst case, we deliver only the main feature.
vocab.example_vi: Trong tình huống xấu nhất, chúng tôi chỉ bàn giao tính năng chính.

vocab.example: With a tight deadline, I speak to my manager on the same day.
vocab.example_vi: Khi hạn chót gấp, tôi trao đổi với quản lý ngay trong ngày.

listening.title: Situational questions in a second interview

lines.speaker: Thanh (Hiring Manager)
lines.text: Let me ask a hypothetical question about a difficult week.

lines.speaker: Linh (Candidate)
lines.text: Please go ahead. I will use a real example if I can.

lines.speaker: Thanh (Hiring Manager)
lines.text: Two managers give you urgent work with the same tight deadline.

lines.speaker: Linh (Candidate)
lines.text: First I check which task affects customers, then I prioritise that one.

lines.speaker: Thanh (Hiring Manager)
lines.text: And if both tasks affect customers in the same way?

lines.speaker: Linh (Candidate)
lines.text: Then I raise it early and ask both managers to decide together.

lines.speaker: Thanh (Hiring Manager)
lines.text: Good. Imagine nobody is available and you must choose alone.

lines.speaker: Linh (Candidate)
lines.text: I think it through, make a judgement call, and write down my reasons.

lines.speaker: Thanh (Hiring Manager)
lines.text: What is the worst case in that situation?

lines.speaker: Linh (Candidate)
lines.text: One manager waits an extra day, so I tell that person immediately.

lines.speaker: Thanh (Hiring Manager)
lines.text: Last one. This clash of priorities happens every month. What then?

lines.speaker: Linh (Candidate)
lines.text: I would suggest one short planning meeting for both teams each Monday.

questions.q: What does Linh check first when two tasks are urgent?
options: Which task is easier to finish

questions.q: What does Linh do when she must decide alone?
options: She waits until the next morning
She thinks it through and writes down her reasons
She finishes both tasks at the same time

questions.q: What does Linh suggest for a clash of priorities that repeats?
options: A short planning meeting for both teams each Monday

shadowing: If two tasks clash, I ask my manager which one to prioritise.
In that situation I would think it through before I answer anyone.
When there is a clash of priorities, I raise it early with my manager.
With a tight deadline, I tell the team about the risk immediately.
It was a judgement call, and I explained my reasons to the team.
